title: SMTO-HTTP-0068 — The request's search or form values aren't in a usable form

html:
SMTO-HTTP-0068 — The request's search or form values aren't in a usable form

GUID: 11c081b6-cc29-40ae-a52f-0f94a6777dc7
Slug: http-fields-invalid
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • Search values in a web address and form values must be simple names with plain values, like text, numbers or true/false. This request had values nested inside other values, or invalid ones, so it wasn't sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to send each search or form value as one plain value, for example status=open, rather than a group of values inside another. Web addresses and forms can only hold simple name-and-value pairs.
  2. If the service expects nested data, ask the Agent to send it as structured content with POST, PUT or PATCH, following the service's documentation. Structured content can hold nested values that search and form values cannot.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's request is sent and returns a result from the service.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, together with what you wanted to search for or submit, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Query or form data was rejected: it is not an object, a field name is not a string or contains control characters, or a value is nested, non-scalar or a non-finite number (NaN or Infinity).

What this means

  • Query/form data is not an object, has invalid field names, nested non-scalar values or non-finite numeric values. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Query/form data is not an object, has invalid field names, nested non-scalar values or non-finite numeric values.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect value types and numeric finiteness; arrays must contain supported scalars.

How to fix it

  • Pass query and form_body as flat objects whose values are strings, finite numbers, booleans, null or arrays of those. Flatten nested objects in the format the endpoint documents (for example filter[status]=open), or send nested data as json_body with a write method.
  • Represent query/form data as an object and replace nested values with the endpoint-supported scalar format.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The endpoint-supported object of scalar fields or scalar arrays encodes correctly.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
